content.title: About
content.content: Beef, roast, hash is a dish made from finely chopped boiled or roasted beef, sautéed with onion, carrot, and spices. It is often served with mashed potatoes or bread and has a rich, savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “hash” comes from the French “hacher” meaning “to chop finely.”
The dish is popular in the United States and Canada, frequently served as a breakfast item.
Traditional recipes used beef tail, but today more common cuts are used for convenience.
Hash is often cooked in large pots, which helps retain the meat’s juiciness.
It is believed to have originated in the 19th century as a way to use leftover meat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef helps supply energy to muscles.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Adding salt or soy sauce can make the dish overly salty.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Improper cooking can lead to salmonella or E. coli contamination.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hash hot, often with a side of mashed potatoes, rice, or fresh vegetables. Adding poached eggs or cheese can enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked hash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
